nodes.description: Congenital anomalies of the heart, left-right patterning, genitourinary tract, gastrointestinal tract, diaphragm, chest wall and face indicate that FRYL dosage matters for morphogenesis in several organ systems. Fryl-null mice die soon after birth with renal tubular defects, and morpholino knockdown of fryl in zebrafish causes cardiac and craniofacial defects. The developmental pathway through which FRYL acts in these tissues is unknown.

nodes.description: The neurodevelopmental features are thought to reflect a requirement for FRYL in neuronal development. Direct evidence comes only from Drosophila: furry is expressed in neurons but not glia, is required for neuronal communication in the retina, and together with the NDR kinase Tricornered limits dendritic branching and enforces dendritic tiling. Whether FRYL acts through NDR kinases in human neurons is untested.
